title: Lateral photovoltaic infrared detectors with colloidal quantum dots - Nature Photonics
byline: Yang; Caillas; Augustin; Feng; Jinlei; Guyot-Sionnest; Philippe
html:
Abstract

Colloidal quantum dots have ushered in solution-processable infrared detectors, promising a low-cost technology for diverse applications. However, their performance, limited by low external quantum efficiency and high noise currents, continues to lag behind state-of-the-art single-crystal devices. Earlier quantum dot photovoltaic detectors used vertical stacks in which the nanoparticle film is sandwiched between conductive electrode layers that limit infrared transmission. Here we show that coating thin films of HgTe quantum dots directly on interdigitated Au/Ti and Pt electrodes, before capping the dots with a protective polymer layer, leverages the asymmetric metal–Hg interactions to create a lateral p–n junction. This approach eliminates the top electrode, creates optical resonances that boost light collection and provides efficient carrier collection by matching the electrode gaps to the carrier diffusion lengths. The resulting detectors, based on mid-wave infrared quantum dots, achieve 70% external quantum efficiency at 4 µm and background-limited performance at 160 K, and retain 95% of their initial performance after seven months. By simply tuning quantum dot size, we further demonstrate spectrally versatile infrared detection across the short- and long-wave regimes.
